families.label: Reservoir storage and elevation
families.period: Dated daily instant; month-end for monthly mode
families.producer: Reclamation operations and DWR CDEC sensor 15 / 6
families.transform: Native acre-feet and feet; no interpolation. Use DATE TIME, not OBS DATE.
families.example: Lake Mead: 6,816,799.80 acre-ft, Oct 12, 2026; a stock, not annual consumption.
families.limits: Provisional; eight Reclamation histories lack Oct1–12,2025. Don Pedro has three missing days.

families.label: Reservoir capacity and percent full
families.quantity: reference capacity; ratio of compatible stock
families.producer: CDEC RES, Reclamation capacity sheet and AOP Table1
families.transform: Stored / stated capacity ×100; federal AOP live+vacant denominators and results marked approximate.
families.limits: Not dependable supply. Seven federal reference capacities are approximate; no precision ranking.

families.label: River gauge discharge
families.period: Observation timestamp; not integrated annual volume
families.transform: Retain native cfs, timestamp and provisional flag.
families.limits: Gauge discharge is not legal apportionment or consumptive use.

families.label: Station snow water equivalent and WY peak
families.period: Latest dated observation; WY2026 peak is maximum valid daily station SWE Oct1,2025–Sep30,2026
families.producer: NRCS WTEQ value / median_1991, SNOTEL Snowpack Update Report seasonal peak medians, and CDEC daily sensor3
families.transform: Retain inches. Reject negative sensor readings; blanks stay null. Compare the observed WY2026 maximum with the source-published median of seasonal peaks from the NRCS SNOTEL Snowpack Update Report, 1991–2020. Preserve shorter normal-record counts, including Agua Canyon’s26years. Daily medians remain separately retained, never relabeled as seasonal peak medians. Peak percent of normal is observed season peak / published station median seasonal peak ×100, rounded to a whole percent; it is not a basin index.
families.example: Berthoud Summit observed WY2026 peak12.2inches on Mar17,2026 beside23.2inches published median seasonal peak, 1991–2020; normal peak date May03. Latest 0.1 inch Oct13,2026. The peak benchmark is53% of the published23.2-inch median, not percent of the15.9-inch daily median on Mar17.
families.limits: NRCS seasonal peak medians are published source statistics, not maxima of daily medians. No CDEC median acquired. Peaks with missing days are observed maxima, not guaranteed seasonal maxima. Stations do not represent whole basins.

families.label: WY2026 monthly exploration
families.producer: Retained daily reservoir and snow series; precomputed per-entity summaries
families.transform: Take only the record on the calendar month’s last day. Missing day gives No reading. No nearest day, averaging, interpolation or annual/12.
families.example: March2026 at Oroville uses Mar31,2026 storage; the card and time caption identify month-end.
families.limits: Annual use and legal context retain their own dates and muted presentation. Geography stays dated. No monthly reservoir elevation or consumptive-use series is implied.

families.label: Lower Colorado entitlement and actual use
families.quantity: Beneficial consumptive entitlement / approved use / source-defined consumption, or explicitly labeled diversion
families.period: Current CY2026 legal/operational context beside actual CY2025; dated source releases
families.producer: Reclamation CY2025 Accounting Report Tables4–6,11; 2026AOP and Part417 approvals; entitlement listings
families.transform: Transcribe exact recipient/quantity and preserve acre-ft. Consumption is mainstream diversions less qualifying returns, not gauge flow. No sum across state and user totals.
families.example: Arizona: 2,800,000 basic less 512,000 shortage+DCP = 2,288,000 acre-ft CY2026. CY2025 consumed 1,910,524. Different years: no delta. CY2025 fully adjusted availability 1,910,524 less same-year consumption 1,910,524 = 0 acre-ft.
families.limits: State outline is orientation, not a spatial adjudication of rights. Fully adjusted availability includes conservation/ICS adjustments; the accounting balance is not a violation or physical-shortage measure. IID’s current approval includes LCWSP and is context only versus older actual. CAP balance is variable. Big Bend contract diversion is not consumption.

families.label: SWP / CVP allocation percentages
families.producer: DWR May15,2026 and Reclamation Aug11,2026 notices
families.transform: Retain source denominator: requested SWP supply vs CVP south-of-Delta irrigation contract total.
families.example: SWP45% requested supply; CVP28% contract total. No cross-project difference.
families.limits: Later supersession clearance incomplete; annual announcement is not a monthly observed value.

families.label: City supply portfolios
families.quantity: reported annual volume categories or rounded narrative shares
families.period: LADWP FY2024/25, Phoenix CY2025, LVVWD report-on-2025 context
families.transform: Keep original periods and denominator. Never normalize a range or infer missing bar values.
families.example: Phoenix surface97–99%, groundwater about2%, retained independently. LADWP groundwater6,107 and recycled13,241 acre-ft.
families.limits: LVVWD90/10 is not an audited volume budget or every SNWA member. LADWP complete shares not tabulated. Recycled environmental reuse excluded.

families.label: Mexico treaty and reduction context
families.quantity: scheduled / allocated delivery, reduction, recoverable savings, conservation
families.period: CY2026 vs adopted CY2027–2028; each has effective dates
families.producer: IBWC Aug15,2025 and Sep9,2026 publications; Minutes323/330/334
families.transform: Keep published initial1,352,595 acre-ft unchanged. Separate 50,000 reduction, 30,000 recoverable savings, and at least67,000 additional conservation in2026.
families.example: Minute334: 250,000 acre-ft/year reduction for Jan1,2027–Dec31,2028. Not a current2026 deduction.
families.limits: Published initial allocation is not silently recomputed from rounded1.5million; treaty-volume/rounding reconciliation remains open. Morelos anchor is approximate regional geography, not surveyed engineering geometry.

families.label: Tribal rights and settlement context
families.quantity: decreed diversion, multi-source settlement budget, or reported consumption with its own recipient
families.period: Each instrument / listing has its own source date
families.producer: Ten Tribes Partnership/Reclamation2018 Ch3; DOJ Gila settlement2023 update; Reclamation2026 entitlement listing and CY2025 accounting
families.transform: Separate sovereign right, infrastructure access and actual use. Do not treat an unquantified right as zero. CA-side tribal facts retain CA-side scope.
families.example: GRIC653,500 acre-ft/year settlement budget includes CAP, Gila, Salt and groundwater. It is not all Colorado River consumption.
families.limits: Not a complete tribal rights register. Six Census reservation outlines are geographic context, not water-rights boundaries.

families.label: Critically overdrafted groundwater basins
families.period: DWR GIS boundary current Dec9,2022; classification2016 with2019 modifications
families.transform: Use21 actual GIS polygons, simplified .004° with topology preservation; no interpolation from wells.
families.example: Kern County subbasin is selectable, with its DWR boundary date and long-term classification.
families.limits: Not current groundwater level, live drought severity, or a modeled depletion quantity.

families.label: Rivers, conveyances, lake outlines and traces
families.producer: USGS NHD, NaturalEarth, DWR SWP reaches, inherited OSM and MWD private reference
families.transform: Source-backed lines with constant width; join exact endpoints only. Trace highlights documented relationships. Label unresolved Oroville outlet and Delta-channel routing breaks; do not invent a bridge.
families.example: Oroville trace includes Feather, Sacramento, Delta, Banks and SWP. Delta channels remain explicitly unresolved.
families.limits: Natural river source geometry is not engineering topology or measured end-to-end delivery. LVVWD remains EPA150-metre inventory-buffer approximation because operator API requires authentication. Unlabeled non-reservoir lakes are plain terrain water.
